summary: Adds a do-nothing NullRunner to the RUNNERS registry so the unchanged workspace→execute→collect→score pipeline can be driven with --agent null, plus a --null-run mode on audit_dataset.py (WS4's script) that reads the null run's summary.yaml per_case, recomputes reward via agent_eval.harbor.reward.compose_reward, and flags non-discriminative cases (bool-judge passes or recomputed reward >= threshold) into dataset_audit.yaml under a null_probe section labeled "null-pass rate (joint task/judge non-discriminativeness, upper-bounds 1−V1)". Documented as optional Step 6.5 in eval-dataset SKILL.md with score.py --samples 3 so stochastic-judge null-passes are majority-voted. Incorporates all 6 mandatory corrections from the v1-2 verdict; all cited anchors re-verified against the working tree (RUNNERS at agent_eval/agent/__init__.py:9-14, --agent at execute.py:191/276-280, --model requirement at execute.py:238-242, per_case merge at score.py:2745 with no stored reward, --samples at score.py:1574-1577/2900, empty-run tolerance at execute.py:934 and collect.py:245-246/352-361).
depends_on: WS4 (v1-1 dataset audit + manifest) — creates skills/eval-dataset/scripts/audit_dataset.py and dataset_audit.yaml; WS5 adds the --null-run mode to that script and merges a null_probe key into that file. Fallback if WS4 is unlanded: WS5 creates audit_dataset.py containing only the null-probe mode under the same conventions (bootstrap import first; scripts/agent_eval symlink already exists), and WS4 merges its checks in later. The NullRunner half of WS5 has no dependency and can land first.

changes.spec: NEW ~55-line stdlib-only module. class NullRunner(EvalRunner): __init__(self, log_prefix=None, **kwargs) stores log_prefix only; classmethod from_config(cls, config, *, log_prefix=None, **overrides) -> NullRunner ignores every config field and every override kwarg (execute.py:1403-1411 passes subagent_model/mlflow_experiment/mlflow_tracking_uri/effort/permissions — all accepted via **overrides and dropped; matches ABC contract at agent_eval/agent/base.py:36-48); property name -> 'null'; property version -> '1' (execute.py:1550 does getattr(runner, 'version', '')); execute(self, target, args, workspace, model, settings_path=None, system_prompt=None, max_budget_usd=5.0, timeout_s=600, extra_env=None) -> RunResult returns immediately without spawning anything: RunResult(exit_code=0, stdout='', stderr='', duration_s=0.0, token_usage=None, cost_usd=0.0, num_turns=0, resolved_model='null'). Edge cases: empty stdout means execute.py:934-946 writes no stdout.log and collect.py:352-361 emits an empty events.json (verified tolerant); cost_usd=0.0 sums cleanly in _sum_reported_costs; num_turns=0 rolls up to num_turns: None and compute_run_metrics skips turn metrics (turns>0 guards); resolved_model='null' makes run_result.json show the probe rather than the ignored --model [verdict C6]; never reads settings_path or touches the workspace, so interception hooks never fire (Step 3a skippable, C6). Module docstring states: diagnostic runner for the solvability probe (docs/paper-validity-analysis.md v1-2), not for real evaluations.

Add `from .null import NullRunner`; add '"null": NullRunner' to the RUNNERS dict (lines 9-14); add 'NullRunner' to __all__. No config.py change needed: runner.type is not validated against RUNNERS (only codex-specific guards at config.py:1508-1516), and execute.py:276-280 accepts any registered key via --agent.

Adds the --null-run mode to WS4's script (or creates the file with only this mode if WS4 is unlanded — then `import agent_eval._bootstrap  # noqa: F401` must be the first import since the script uses yaml + agent_eval; the scripts/agent_eval symlink already exists) [C1]. Constant NULL_PROBE_LABEL = 'null-pass rate (joint task/judge non-discriminativeness, upper-bounds 1−V1)' [C5]. Functions: (a) _bool_passes(per_judge: dict) -> list[dict] — a judge counts as a pass iff isinstance(rec.get('value'), bool) and rec['value'] and no 'error' key; if:-skipped records (value None, rationale 'Skipped: ...', score.py:1555-1559), condition-error records (value None + error, score.py:1565-1570), and errored records (score.py:1600) never count [C3]; numeric 1 never counts (bool isinstance); returns [{judge, rationale, judge_type, stability?}]. (b) _confidence(name, rec, config, registry_kinds) -> str [C4] — 'majority-of-N' when rec['stability']['samples']>1; 'deterministic' for judge_type check/code and builtin judges whose registry kind is python; 'single-sample (builtin LLM judges are never sampled)' for builtin-llm (CLI --samples applies only to llm/agent, score.py:1574); 'single-sample (rerun score.py with --samples 3)' for llm/agent without stability; 'unknown' when BuiltinJudgeRegistry discovery fails (tolerated, lazy). (c) _recompute_reward(per_judge, config) -> float [C2] — from agent_eval.harbor.reward import compose_reward, judge_ranges; reward, _ = compose_reward(per_judge, judge_ranges=judge_ranges(config), reward_cfg=config.reward); per_case records already match the {name: {value, error?}} shape compose_reward consumes (extra rationale/stability/step keys ignored by it); reward is NOT read from summary.yaml. (d) default_reward_threshold(config) -> tuple[float, str] [C3] — candidates from config.thresholds[judge]['min_mean']: feedback_type=='bool' judges clamp(min_mean,0,1); numeric judges normalize over declared JudgeConfig.score_range (fallback config.reward.effective_score_range if reward set, else [1,5]; span<=0 skipped); if config.reward.judge names a candidate use it alone (clamped not normalized when reward.normalize is false, mirroring compose_reward's clamp path); else mean of candidates; else (0.5, 'default (no thresholds.min_mean declared)'); source string is printed and persisted. (e) audit_null_run(run_dir: Path, config, dataset_root: Path, reward_threshold: float|None) -> dict — loads <run_dir>/summary.yaml; missing file or missing per_case key -> stderr guidance ('score the null run first: score.py judges --run-id <id> --samples 3'; notes the batch-mode zero-artifact limitation) + sys.exit(2); per case computes bool_passes, recomputed reward, null_pass = bool(bool_passes) or reward >= threshold, reasons list; warns on per_case judges absent from config.judges (drift — ranges fall back); dataset case dirs absent from per_case listed as not_audited; returns {run_id, run_dir, generated_at (UTC ISO), reward_threshold, reward_threshold_source, statistic: {label: NULL_PROBE_LABEL, null_pass_cases, audited_cases, rate}, not_audited, cases: {case_id: {null_pass, reward (round 4), reasons, bool_passes?: [{judge, rationale, judge_type, confidence, stability?}]}}} — flagged bool judges carry their stability dict so sampled-vote evidence is surfaced [C4]. (f) write_null_probe(dataset_root, null_probe) — merge into <dataset_root>/dataset_audit.yaml preserving WS4's keys, replacing the null_probe key wholesale. CLI: --null-run <run-dir> (Path) + --reward-threshold <float> added to the parser; when --null-run present only this mode runs; exit 0 with findings (findings-not-verdicts), exit 2 on usage/summary errors. Console output prints the labeled rate, per-flagged-case judge+confidence+rationale lines, the threshold with its source, and the triage line: 'each null-pass is either a degenerate case (fix the case) or a vacuous/lenient judge (fix the judge); the judge's rationale distinguishes them.'

New '## Step 6.5: Null-agent solvability probe (optional — run once per dataset revision, before the first real /eval-run)' inserted between Step 6 (line 200) and Step 7 (line 215). Contains: what it measures with the exact NULL_PROBE_LABEL caveat — under LLM judges this is a joint task/judge probe, NOT the paper's pure-V1 38% figure [C5]; cost note (zero agent tokens; LLM judges still run, ×3 samples); the 5-command sequence using ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/eval-run/scripts/ paths (eval-anova SKILL.md:68 precedent): 1) workspace.py --config <config> --run-id <null-run-id> with note that eval-run Step 3a interception resolution is skippable because nothing executes [C6]; 2) execute.py --config <config> --workspace <ws> --model <any> --agent null --output $AGENT_EVAL_RUNS_DIR/<eval-name>/<null-run-id> --run-id <null-run-id> with note that --model (or models.skill) is still required by execute.py (execute.py:238-242) but ignored by the null runner [C6]; 3) collect.py (expect the normal 'no artifacts collected' warning); 4) score.py judges --run-id <null-run-id> --config <config> --samples 3 (majority-votes stochastic judges) [C4]; 5) audit_dataset.py --config <config> --null-run <run-dir>. Also: run-id convention null-probe-<YYYYMMDD>; fix-the-case vs fix-the-judge interpretation with the consulted_docs vacuous-PASS example (agent_eval/judges/process/consulted_docs.py:60); explicit batch-mode limitation (zero artifacts -> no run case dirs -> score.py _get_case_dirs exits; probe currently requires case-mode scoring). Step 7 report list gains a 'Null probe (if run): null-pass rate + flagged cases' bullet.

open_questions: Batch-mode datasets: a null run produces zero artifacts, so collect.py's batch branch creates no run case dirs and score.py _get_case_dirs exits 1 — the probe therefore only works for case-mode scoring today. Accept the documented limitation (audit exits 2 with guidance, as planned), or extend collect.py to always create run case dirs in batch mode (small change to shared collection code, benefits beyond the probe)?

Audit exit code on findings: keep exit 0 always (probe outputs findings, not verdicts — the proposal's own framing), or add an opt-in --fail-on-null-pass flag so CI can gate dataset revisions on a zero null-pass rate?
